title: Dedicated capacity weekly sync - prep + follow-ups
content:
Meeting: Dedicated capacity weekly sync - prep notes and follow-ups
Owner: Kayla Patel (notes for 1:1 + weekly)
Date: 2026-03-04 weekly sync (prep started 2026-02-25)
Attendees (expected): Ethan, Maya, Liam, ops on-call (TBD)
Context / goals:
- Quick check on current reserved capacity vs committed customers. Surface any shortages and near-term scheduling conflicts.
- Review autoscaling behavior last week (burst events + scale-up latency).
- Finalize recommendation for Q2 reservations (A100/H100 mix) to present to finance next Wed.
- Confirm action owners for follow-ups (procurement, infra, SRE).

High-level numbers (current snapshot):
- Total reserved GPUs (prod pools): 120 A100-80GB equiv (pool-a: 50, pool-b: 40, pool-c: 30)
- On-demand burst capacity configured: extra 24 H100 (spot-like) via cloud bursts
- Average utilization (prod pools) last 7 days: 64% overall; peak observed: 89% (2026-02-20 15:34 UTC, billing spike from Partner-X)
- Queue/backpressure events: 3 incidents last week, mostly short (<90s) but noticeable for low-latency SLAs

Observations / issues to raise:
1) Pool fragmentation: pool-b under heavy tail traffic for long-context chat models (ctx=8k), leading to uneven KV-cache memory churn. We may need pool rebalancing or dedicated long-seq nodes.
2) Autoscale latency: scale-up cold-starts ~2.5m on average when launching H100 instances in region-us-west. This violates soft SLO (<=90s) for dedicated customers. Likely causes: instance warm-up + model load times.
3) Reservation sizing: current Q1 commit usage trending +12% vs forecast; finance asking for conservative commit for Q2 to avoid over-commit penalties.
4) Cost optimization opportunity: shift some non-critical batch workloads to quantized variants on A100 rather than H100 to lower unit cost by ~22%. Need impact eval on latency/quality.

Agenda (15m total):
- 2m quick sync (this doc highlights)
- 5m metrics review (utilization, incidents) — Maya
- 4m autoscale root-cause updates + mitigation plan — Ethan/Liam
- 3m Q2 reservation recommendation (numbers + risk) — Kayla
- 1m assign follow-ups and dates

Key data points to show live:
- Dashboard: per-pool token/sec, per-model p99 latency (console link in slack)
- Incident timeline for 2026-02-20 spike (logs + traces)
- Cost delta table: A100 vs H100 for common workloads (quick table below)

Quick back-of-envelope cost table (for slides):
- H100 baseline unit cost (on-reserve effective): $X.XX / GPU-hour (use finance number before presentation)
- A100 quantized throughput => ~0.78x tokens/sec vs H100, but 0.78*cost => ~22% lower unit cost for batch reranking jobs
(Need finance to confirm exact rates — action for Liam)

Draft Q2 reservations proposal (numbers to refine):
- Option A (conservative): +20 A100 net (total 140), keep H100 burst pool at 24.
- Option B (balanced): +10 A100 + 8 H100 (total 130 A100 equiv + 32 H100 burst).
- Option C (aggressive): +30 A100 + convert 8 H100 to reserved H100 (for low-latency customers).
Recommendation: start with Option B, but attach a 60-day review clause; aim to keep budget delta within +10% of current committed spend.

Risks & questions (for discussion):
- If we move to Option B, will procurement/finance sign off on mixed reservations? (Finance contact: sara.kim@redwood)
- Can SRE reduce cold-start model load times by pre-warming lightweight containers? (PR#914 is a warmup shim — need SRE sign-off)
- How to avoid noisy-neighbor impact when long-context models burst? Consider priority queues or dedicated long-seq pool.

Action items (owner / due):
- Kayla: finalize Option B proposal doc + cost delta table, attach to Confluence and share with finance by 2026-03-06 (linked_artifacts: Confluence page).
- Liam: confirm real unit cost numbers with finance, update cost table, assign JIRA ticket JIRA-RED-1427 (due 2026-03-05).
- Ethan: run targeted test of pre-warm shim from PR#914 in us-west staging, measure scale-up latency; report by 2026-03-03 (status: in_progress).
- Maya: prepare per-pool utilization slides for meeting, include peak incident trace screenshots (due 2026-03-04 morning).
- SRE (TBD): evaluate dedicated long-seq node config and rough capacity needed for 8k+ contexts (estimate due 2026-03-10).

Notes to self / talking points:
- Emphasize we prefer conservative commit but need agility — propose 60-day review on any new reservation.
- Highlight cost-savings path with quantization for batch jobs to reduce pressure on H100 pools.
- Call out the customer impact: low-latency SLA customers noticed degraded experience during the 02-20 spike; we cannot defer mitigation for long.

Unresolved follow-ups / parking lot:
- Need concrete perf delta matrix for A100 vs H100 across our top-5 models (Maya to coordinate with Applied-ML).
- Confirm block booking windows for procurement to get best reserved pricing.
- Check if any enterprise customers are scheduling big evals in mid-March (could drive burst).

Tomorrow / next week prep:
- If we approve Option B, schedule a 30-min ops-runbook session to update canary policies and fallback routes (owner: Kayla).
- Prepare short customer-facing note (if required) explaining planned capacity increases and expected SLA improvements (owner: CS to draft after decision).

End of notes.

-- Kayla
(p.s. keep this doc rough; will move polished proposal to Confluence once numbers confirmed)
